authorization: User asked what the older-adult result becomes with the model trained with assumed-100 normal gait.
question: On the same 58 older-cohort people and windows as the 2026-11-03 frozen test, how do scores change with the LJMU100-mixed model?
input: D:/gait-research-data/D_P/frozen-transfer-and-deviation-20261103/features.npz unchanged: 3D markers projected to a virtual side camera. Not real video.
models: studies/20261104-ljmu100-mixed: baseline (Stanford only) and mixed (Stanford + LJMU 64 people 881 records assumed 100). Fixed bundle/ensemble.json fusion, all five folds averaged.
primary_calibration: Stanford-training-only member calibration, the condition reported in the paper draft.
aggregation: Same as frozen test: window -> primary record mean -> person mean of left/right.
primary_population: Age>=65 healthy 11 and stroke 25 with primary windows.
outcomes: healthy-stroke mean difference with 10000 person bootstrap
25 stroke people: Spearman with POMA and speed, speed-partial Spearman with POMA
interpretation_limits: This cohort was already inspected on 2026-11-03, so this is a post-hoc exploratory comparison. No measured GDI exists for these inputs, so higher scores are not accuracy. A difference between groups is not diagnostic performance.
